market.question: Will the Democrats win the South Carolina Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm South Carolina U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

market.question: Will **real GDP** increase by more than 4.0% in Q3 2026? (Above 4.0%)
market.rules:

The market will expire at the first 10:00 AM following the release of the data for Q3 2026, or 3 months following that expected date of data release. Please note the Expiration Value is the one-decimal value published by the BEA.

recent_facts.fact: On October 8, 2026, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate of Q3 2026 real GDP growth was 3.6% (SAAR), down from 3.7% on October 6. A wholesale trade report cut the estimated contribution of inventory investment from 2.07 to 1.98 percentage points.
Components in the October 8 GDPNow: net exports contribute -2.69 pp (vs -2.59 pp before), real consumer spending growth is 3.4% and real gross private domestic investment growth is 21.5%.

In late September, GDPNow fell to 3.7% from 5.0% after the August trade report. The August goods deficit was $132.6B, against $115.0B expected and $118.9B in July. The net exports contribution went from -1.37 pp to -2.60 pp, and consumer spending growth was cut from 4.2% to 3.5%.
The GDPNow Q3 2026 nowcast was 5.0% on September 25, 2026. Earlier in the quarter (August) it had been near or above 6%, then dropped to 4.3% according to Crypto Briefing reports.
The BEA third estimate put Q2 2026 real GDP growth at 2.2% annualized, up from 1.5% in the second estimate (the advance estimate was also 1.5%). Q1 2026 was revised to 2.5%.

recent_facts.source: MTS Insights (New York Fed Staff Nowcast)
recent_facts.fact: For Q2 2026, the final NY Fed Staff Nowcast was 2.9%, but the BEA advance estimate on July 30 came in at 1.5%, a miss of 1.4 pp.

The question resolves on the one-decimal, seasonally adjusted annualized real GDP growth rate in BEA's Advance Estimate. It resolves Yes only if that figure is strictly above 4.0, so a print of exactly 4.0 resolves No.

market.question: Perim Island no longer under Houthi control by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Perim Island is no longer under Houthi control by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

“The Houthis” refers to the Houthi movement (Ansar Allah), including its governing institutions and any armed force operating under its direction or on its behalf. “Perim Island” refers to Perim (Mayyun) Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen.

“No longer under the control of the Houthis” means that the Houthis no longer exercise primary military control over Perim Island, and another state, occupying force, the internationally recognized government of Yemen, or an internationally backed authority has established control over the island.

Temporary raids, isolated landings, special operations, bombardment, sabotage, naval presence offshore, or temporary disruption of Houthi activity will not qualify on their own.

An announcement, threat, or claim that the Houthis have lost control will not qualify without actual control being established.

If control changes pursuant to a negotiated settlement, ceasefire term, surrender, or transfer agreement, this will qualify only once actual control has been established on the island.

If control over Perim Island is contested, unclear, disputed, or not sufficiently established by the resolution date, this will not qualify, and the market will resolve to “No”.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the relevant governments and militaries, along with a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In recent Ohio governor polls, Democrat Amy Acton led in five: CNN/SSRS (Sep 29–Oct 5, 760 likely voters) had Acton 50%, Ramaswamy 42%. NYT/Siena (Sep 22–Oct 1, 616 likely voters) had Acton 49%, Ramaswamy 45%. YouGov (Sep 18–30, 3,777 likely voters) had Acton 48%, Ramaswamy 44%. Suffolk (Sep 23–27, 500 voters) had Acton 50%, Ramaswamy 41%. Marist (Sep 24–27, 1,298 registered voters) had Acton 50%, Ramaswamy 44%.

Republican Vivek Ramaswamy led 45% to 43% in a co/efficient poll (Oct 5–6, 925 likely voters, margin of error ±3.49). In that poll, 8% were undecided and 3% backed the Libertarian. It was the only recent poll cited with Ramaswamy ahead.
Pollsmax's polling average across 27 polls has Acton 47.1% and Ramaswamy 45.1%, an Acton lead of 2.0 points. RealClearPolling's average had Acton ahead by 3.8 points in early October.
Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball both rate the Ohio governor race a Toss-up.

In Ohio, final RealClearPolitics averages understated the Republican margin in 4 of 4 recent cases cited. Trump led polls by 2.2 and won by 8.1 (2016), led by 1.0 and won by 8.2 (2020), and led by 9.3 and won by 11.2 (2024). In the 2024 Senate race, Moreno led by 1.7 and won by 3.6. This is one outlet's comparison of averages, not a formal study.
Trump won Ohio by 8 points in both 2016 and 2020, and by 11 points in 2024.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (recalled background, unverified in this research)
recent_facts.fact: Unverified: Democrats last won the Ohio governorship in 2006 (Ted Strickland), and Republicans have won the last four races (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022). Mike DeWine won in 2018 by about 3.7 points and in 2022 by about 25 points.

The Republican ticket is Vivek Ramaswamy with running mate Rob McColley. The Democratic ticket is Amy Acton with running mate David Pepper. Incumbent Republican Mike DeWine is term-limited. The election is November 3, 2026.
Acton has turned down debate invitations, including a CNN debate that Ramaswamy accepted. On Sep 2 her campaign said her focus was talking with Ohioans, not 'platforming a scam artist.'

Coverage of the Marist and Suffolk polls in early October reported that Acton's lead over Ramaswamy had grown compared with earlier polls. Earlier in the cycle, some polls, including Bowling Green, had the race a dead heat or Ramaswamy up 1.

Acton reported a record fundraising haul but still trailed Ramaswamy's $12.9 million cash on hand in the filing period covered (exact date unclear). The article also notes the two campaigns used different cutoff dates and accounting methods.
Early in-person and absentee voting in Ohio began October 6 and runs through November 1. Absentee ballot requests are due by 8:30 p.m. October 27, and Election Day is November 3.

The question resolves when AP, Fox News, and NBC all call the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification. Independents do not count as Democrats even if they are affiliated with the party.

That is roughly 3.2–3.7% above the $80,000 strike, with about 5.5 days (~130 hours) to resolution.

Earlier in October, BTC fell from near $86,600 to an intraday low of about $80,350, only about 0.4% above the $80,000 strike, then partly recovered. In the latest sell-off it dropped from about $85,700 to $82,500 and traded near $82,500 on Oct 9–10.

The 10-year US Treasury yield reached about 5.25%, with some estimates above 5.3%, and oil rose above $101 per barrel. Spot Bitcoin ETFs had about $487M in net outflows on Oct 7, the largest single-day withdrawal since late June.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $115 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will BTC trimmed mean be above $87500.00 by 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026? (Above $87,500.00)
market.rules:
If the price of BTC after issuance and through 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026 is ever above $
87500.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
At each minute throughout the market duration, a settlement value is calculated using every minute-by-minute CF BRTI price for BTC. For each of these individual minute-by-minute checks, the top 20% and bottom 20% of the cumulative dataset are removed before calculating the average of the remaining values. If the trimmed mean associated with any single minute during the period is above the threshold, the market resolves to Yes. This methodology reduces the impact of extreme price spikes or drops. The measurement period runs from when the market is issued until the specified end time. If CF Benchmarks data is unavailable or incomplete at the expiration time, affected strikes resolve to No. For cryptocurrencies with multiple versions, the Exchange will specify which version or ticker is being tracked.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: A Faktor Plus poll (n=986) put the Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia list at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%, an 11.5-point gap. SPS–JS had 4.9% and NADA 2.8%. Faktor Plus's director said the figures could shift during the campaign.

A New Serbian Political Thought (NSPM) survey had the Student List at 44.4% and Vučić's list at 41.7%, a 2.7-point Student List lead. Its authors noted that the fieldwork predates several later campaign developments.

A CRTA/Stanford Democracy Action Lab poll fielded in June 2026 (n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and the SNS-led list at 35.7% among decided voters, with SPS at 3.8% and no other party over the threshold. 12% were undecided and 9% said they would not vote.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election)
recent_facts.fact: All seven 2026 polls listed show a pollster split. Faktor Plus has had SNS ahead every time: by 19.7 (Apr; the page's figures, 46.4 vs 28.7, give 17.7), 16.4 (Jun), 15.7 (Sep 4) and 11.5 points (Sep 21). NSPM (Jul: 39.6 vs 37.5; Sep 30: 44.4 vs 41.7) and CRTA (Jul: 44.9 vs 35.7) have had the Student List ahead. The page lists no October 2026 poll.

Polling this cycle is disputed: opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. Tabloids reported an Ipsos figure (49.1% ruling list vs 9.2% Student List) that Ipsos did not publish; it appears to date from 2025 and is unconfirmed.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September 2026 after SNS nominated him for prime minister and as head of the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list, which is No. 1 on the ballot. The list submitted 209,130 support signatures, compared with 69,099 for the Student List.

The opposition People's Serbia list (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew on 22 September and backed the Student List. PSG had also left the European Serbia alliance in September to support the Student List. European Serbia (PES, Tepić/Ponoš) and NADA are still running separately, so part of the opposition vote is split.

18 lists were submitted and one was withdrawn. The main non-SNS lists are the Student List – Students Are Winning (headed by Ilija Srdanović), Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability! (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), PES and NADA, plus several minority lists. Minority lists are exempt from the 3% threshold. Debates ran from 24 September to 9 October.

Thousands of supporters marched from the University of Belgrade Rectorate to the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) to register the 'Student List – Students Win'. The list fields a full 250 candidates, including Dejan Bodiroga and former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić.

In the 29 March 2026 local elections in 10 municipalities, SNS-led lists won all 10, some narrowly: Kula 51.35% vs 48.65% (19 seats to 18), Aranđelovac about 53% vs 44.9%, Sevojno 51.5% vs 44.8%. Student-backed lists won an estimated 30–50%, and the opposition reported many irregularities.
In the last parliamentary election (December 2023), the SNS-led list won 129 of 250 seats, a majority, with about 47–48% of the vote. The opposition SPN list came second with about 24%.
Unverified, from memory: the SNS-led list has won the most seats in each of the last 6 Serbian parliamentary elections (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023).

Voting is on 25 October 2026 for all 250 seats, elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. The election was called on 9 September after early dissolution; the regular date would have been by December 2027. RIK publishes the official results.

recent_facts.fact: All-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months to August 2026, the same as July. The August 2026 NSA index was 334.980 (1982-84=100).

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index, which is the base for the September 2026 year-over-year figure, was 324.800. The August 2025 index was 323.976, so the NSA rise from August to September 2025 was about 0.25%.

recent_facts.source: Research desk calculation from BLS index levels
recent_facts.fact: For a published 12-month rate of 3.7% or more (a rate of at least 3.65%), the September 2026 NSA index must reach about 336.655. That is an NSA month-over-month gain of about 0.50% or more from August's 334.980. A gain of about 0.40% would give roughly 3.55%, which BLS would publish as 3.6%.
BLS will release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day, one minute before the release.
AAA reported that the national average gasoline price for September 2026 was $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023).
Citing EIA data, LendingTree put the average price of regular gasoline at $4.36/gal in September 2026, up from $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is about a 7.4% rise from August to September.

Gas prices peaked at $4.48 on September 24, the highest for that time of year. The national average then fell to $4.36 by October 8. AAA linked the high prices to volatility around the Strait of Hormuz and crude oil at about $90–100 per barrel.

In August 2026, energy CPI rose 2.1% from the prior month and 16.3% over the year. Gasoline rose 27.4% year over year, and its NSA price was up 2.5% in August. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year, down from 2.5% in July.
Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items changes in 2026: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%.

A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. recent_facts.fact: A Faktor Plus poll (n=986) put the Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia list at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%, an 11.5-point gap. SPS–JS had 4.9% and NADA 2.8%. Faktor Plus's director said the figures could shift during the campaign.

A New Serbian Political Thought (NSPM) survey had the Student List at 44.4% and Vučić's list at 41.7%, a 2.7-point Student List lead. Its authors noted that the fieldwork predates several later campaign developments.

A CRTA/Stanford Democracy Action Lab poll fielded in June 2026 (n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and the SNS-led list at 35.7% among decided voters, with SPS at 3.8% and no other party over the threshold. 12% were undecided and 9% said they would not vote.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election)
recent_facts.fact: All seven 2026 polls listed show a pollster split. Faktor Plus has had SNS ahead every time: by 19.7 (Apr; the page's figures, 46.4 vs 28.7, give 17.7), 16.4 (Jun), 15.7 (Sep 4) and 11.5 points (Sep 21). NSPM (Jul: 39.6 vs 37.5; Sep 30: 44.4 vs 41.7) and CRTA (Jul: 44.9 vs 35.7) have had the Student List ahead. The page lists no October 2026 poll.

Polling this cycle is disputed: opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. Tabloids reported an Ipsos figure (49.1% ruling list vs 9.2% Student List) that Ipsos did not publish; it appears to date from 2025 and is unconfirmed.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September 2026 after SNS nominated him for prime minister and as head of the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list, which is No. 1 on the ballot. The list submitted 209,130 support signatures, compared with 69,099 for the Student List.

The opposition People's Serbia list (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew on 22 September and backed the Student List. PSG had also left the European Serbia alliance in September to support the Student List. European Serbia (PES, Tepić/Ponoš) and NADA are still running separately, so part of the opposition vote is split.

18 lists were submitted and one was withdrawn. The main non-SNS lists are the Student List – Students Are Winning (headed by Ilija Srdanović), Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability! (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), PES and NADA, plus several minority lists. Minority lists are exempt from the 3% threshold. Debates ran from 24 September to 9 October.

Thousands of supporters marched from the University of Belgrade Rectorate to the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) to register the 'Student List – Students Win'. The list fields a full 250 candidates, including Dejan Bodiroga and former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić.

In the 29 March 2026 local elections in 10 municipalities, SNS-led lists won all 10, some narrowly: Kula 51.35% vs 48.65% (19 seats to 18), Aranđelovac about 53% vs 44.9%, Sevojno 51.5% vs 44.8%. Student-backed lists won an estimated 30–50%, and the opposition reported many irregularities.
In the last parliamentary election (December 2023), the SNS-led list won 129 of 250 seats, a majority, with about 47–48% of the vote. The opposition SPN list came second with about 24%.
Unverified, from memory: the SNS-led list has won the most seats in each of the last 6 Serbian parliamentary elections (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023).

Voting is on 25 October 2026 for all 250 seats, elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. The election was called on 9 September after early dissolution; the regular date would have been by December 2027. RIK publishes the official results.

market.question: Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between Oman and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between Oman and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian or Omani policies, obligations, or commitments aimed at managing, permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, including agreements defining vessel traffic corridors, fee collection policies, or other management policies.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Oman and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Tennessee Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Tennessee U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Tennessee)
recent_facts.fact: Democratic nominee Marquita Bradshaw won the August 6 primary with 186,230 votes (54.8%), ahead of Maria Brewer (61,061, 18.0%). Incumbent Republican Bill Hagerty was unopposed in his primary and received 629,194 votes, about 2.5 times the 339,926 cast in the Democratic primary.

The only general-election poll listed is Targoz Market Research's, dated August 26, 2026, of 1,200 registered voters. It had Hagerty at 51% and Bradshaw at 31%, so Hagerty led by 20 points and 18% were undecided or backing another candidate.

recent_facts.source: smarter.vote (Beacon Center survey, as summarized in search results)
recent_facts.fact: Another source reports an August 26 Beacon Center survey with Hagerty at 58% and Bradshaw at 33%. This could not be checked against the Pollsmax listing, which shows different numbers for the same date, so it is unverified.
Hagerty had more than $5 million on hand. None of the four Democrats on the primary ballot raised more than $10,000. Bradshaw is facing Hagerty for the second time after losing to him in 2020.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2020 United States Senate election in Tennessee)
recent_facts.fact: In the 2020 race between the same two candidates, Hagerty won 1,840,926 votes (62.2%) to Bradshaw's 1,040,691 (35.2%), a margin of about 27 points. Independents took about 2.6%.
Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate race in Tennessee since 1990, so Republicans have won every Tennessee Senate election for more than 30 years.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Tennessee)
recent_facts.fact: Besides Hagerty and Bradshaw, the page lists declared independent and third-party candidates, including Andrew Woodruff Mixon of the Federalist Party. It does not say which of them qualified for the ballot.

The general election is November 3, 2026, and Tennessee has no runoff. The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, or on official certification if they do not.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: All-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months to August 2026, the same as July. The August 2026 NSA index was 334.980 (1982-84=100).

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index, which is the base for the September 2026 year-over-year figure, was 324.800. The August 2025 index was 323.976, so the NSA rise from August to September 2025 was about 0.25%.

recent_facts.source: Research desk calculation from BLS index levels
recent_facts.fact: For a published 12-month rate of 3.7% or more (a rate of at least 3.65%), the September 2026 NSA index must reach about 336.655. That is an NSA month-over-month gain of about 0.50% or more from August's 334.980. A gain of about 0.40% would give roughly 3.55%, which BLS would publish as 3.6%.
BLS will release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day, one minute before the release.
AAA reported that the national average gasoline price for September 2026 was $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023).
Citing EIA data, LendingTree put the average price of regular gasoline at $4.36/gal in September 2026, up from $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is about a 7.4% rise from August to September.

Gas prices peaked at $4.48 on September 24, the highest for that time of year. The national average then fell to $4.36 by October 8. AAA linked the high prices to volatility around the Strait of Hormuz and crude oil at about $90–100 per barrel.

In August 2026, energy CPI rose 2.1% from the prior month and 16.3% over the year. Gasoline rose 27.4% year over year, and its NSA price was up 2.5% in August. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year, down from 2.5% in July.
Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items changes in 2026: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: On Oct 10, a US fighter jet disabled the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM said the ship tried to run 'the ongoing naval blockade against Iran.' CENTCOM says that since the blockade resumed on July 14 it has disabled four commercial vessels, turned back 135 ships and destroyed 10 IRGC-linked tankers.

Iranian FM Araghchi said Iran had received Washington's response to its seven-day Hormuz reopening plan and was reviewing it, with messages passing through intermediaries (Qatar among them). Trump said Witkoff was making progress and an agreement could be close, while insisting Iran must not get nuclear weapons. As of about Oct 9 the blockade and sanctions were still in place.

The US has set new demands for a deal. Vance wants a 'meaningful' cut in Iran's uranium enrichment capacity, and Rubio says Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. The article reports no US statement or timeline on lifting the blockade. Iran's plan calls for the US to lift the blockade and oil sanctions and release frozen assets, with Hormuz reopening after 7 days and nuclear talks to follow.

Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not open until Iran's seven conditions, based on the Islamabad memorandum, are met. Lifting the US blockade is one of those conditions.

Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal presented around the UN General Assembly (lift the blockade, oil sanctions waivers, a regional ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, then nuclear talks), but told Axios he expected talks that week. Mediated US-Iran talks took place at UNGA around Sept 23.

Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September, down from about 250,000 bpd in August, the first such month since the war began in February. Separately, an Oct 3 report said the Pentagon is sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf.

Precedent from the first phase: the blockade began Apr 13 and lasted about 9 weeks. On June 14 Trump announced a deal and said he had authorized lifting the blockade, but CENTCOM kept it in place until signing. The MOU was signed June 17 and CENTCOM announced the blockade removed June 18. There was one lifting in roughly 6 months of blockade.

On about May 29, Trump declared he was lifting the naval blockade before any deal was signed. Iranian officials denied a final agreement, and the blockade continued until mid-June. Trump has previously announced a lifting ahead of a finalized deal.

Trump reinstated the blockade on July 13 (effective July 14, 4 PM ET) after the June 17 MOU broke down amid Iranian attacks on shipping and US bases and Iran's claim to have closed the strait. He also announced a 20% fee on cargo through the strait.

The IRGC said it struck the LPG carrier NV Sunshine for using an 'illegal route' and claimed Iran had 'taken control of the administration of the strait.' Sen. Chris Murphy questioned the US strikes and said the blockade is being used as leverage for a deal.
The US midterm elections are on Nov 3, 2026, after the question closes on Oct 31. No signing date, meeting or deadline for a US-Iran agreement had been publicly scheduled as of Oct 11.

In June, both Trump's statement on June 14 that he had authorized lifting the blockade and CENTCOM's announcement on June 18 that it was removed were official US announcements. Under the rules, a declarative presidential announcement of a decision to lift may count even if CENTCOM implements it later.

This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Nov 1, 2026? (Before Nov 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

recent_facts.fact: The Rays will play the Cleveland Guardians in the 2026 ALCS. Cleveland beat the Chicago White Sox in the winner-take-all ALDS Game 5 at Progressive Field on Oct 10, helped by a Jose Ramirez home run.

Tampa Bay swept the Yankees 3-0 in the ALDS, winning 1-0 on Oct 3, 5-2 on Oct 5 and 4-3 on Oct 7 at Yankee Stadium. It was the first sweep in a best-of-five or longer postseason series in franchise history.
The Rays went 98-64 in the regular season, won the AL East and entered the playoffs as the AL's No. 1 seed with a first-round bye.

The best-of-seven ALCS schedule: Games 1-2 on Oct 12-13 at Tropicana Field, Games 3-5 on Oct 15-17 at Progressive Field, and Games 6-7, if needed, on Oct 19-20 at Tropicana Field. Tampa Bay has home-field advantage.

The Rays went 5-1 against the Guardians in the 2026 regular season. In past postseasons, Cleveland leads the matchup 2-1: it won the 2022 AL Wild Card Series 2-0, and Tampa Bay won the 2013 AL Wild Card Game.
In their six regular-season games, the Rays outscored Cleveland 20-8.

The tentative World Series schedule starts with Game 1 on Friday, Oct 23, 2026, and puts a possible Game 7 on Saturday, Oct 31, 2026. A Game 7 that night would start close to the question's close time of Oct 31 at 23:55 UTC (7:55 p.m. ET).

The NLCS is Milwaukee Brewers vs. Los Angeles Dodgers. It begins Oct 11 in Milwaukee, which has home-field advantage, and a Game 7 if needed would be Oct 19. The Rays would face the NL champion if they win the ALCS.

market.question: Will the highest single-day number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz be more than 4 from Oct 5, 2026 to Oct 11, 2026? (Above 4)
market.rules:
If the highest single-day number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 4 from Oct 5, 2026 to Oct 11, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The Expiration Value is determined by identifying the highest single-day count from Oct 5, 2026 to Oct 11, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

recent_facts.fact: As of Oct 11, 2026, the most recent day IMF PortWatch has published for Hormuz is Oct 4, at 4 transits (pre-crisis norm about 85/day). PortWatch has published nothing yet for Oct 5–11.

PortWatch updates weekly, usually on Tuesdays, about two days behind, so the newest Hormuz day is typically 2–9 days old. Data for Oct 5–11 is therefore likely to appear around Tuesday Oct 13, when the market can resolve. PortWatch counts only ships broadcasting on AIS, so tankers sailing with transponders off are missed.

hormuz.now's own AIS daily totals for Oct 5–11 were: Oct 5: 17, Oct 6: 7, Oct 7: 12, Oct 8: 10, Oct 9: 12, Oct 10: 6, Oct 11 (partial at 11:52 UTC): 3. This tracker usually counts more ships than PortWatch, e.g. Oct 2: 12 AIS vs 4 PortWatch, and Oct 4: 10 AIS vs 4 PortWatch.

In PortWatch daily counts for Monday–Sunday weeks, 8 of the last 9 weeks (Aug 3–Oct 4) had at least one day above 4. Weekly highs: 10, 9, 7, 7, 6, 8, 7, 5, 4. The only week that peaked at 4 or less was the most recent one, Sep 28–Oct 4.
PortWatch daily counts for Sep 21–Oct 4 were 2, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 1, 4, 1, 4, 0, 4, 2, 4. The last day above 4 was Sep 24, with 5.
PortWatch monthly average daily transits in 2026: March 3.2, April 7.1, May 3.9, June 12.9, July 10.2. August and September daily values mostly ranged from 1 to 10.
Hormuz transits averaged 3.17/day over Sep 1–6, 2026, with daily counts between 2 and 6, against an 85.5/day average in 2025.
